title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
corePattern: Two Pointers with Fixed Gap + Dummy Sentinel Node
interviewTips: Ask if n is always valid: is 1 <= n <= length guaranteed, and what to do if not?
Mention why dummy node is needed: it unifies removal of head and middle nodes without special-case branching
Trade-off to discuss: two-pass counting is simpler to verify, one-pass two-pointer is optimal for streaming / single traversal follow-up
Edge-case tip: explicitly walk through removing head (n == length) and single-node list ([1], n=1 -> [])

approaches.name: Approach 1: Two-Pass Count Length
approaches.intuition: If we knew the total length L, the nth node from end is the (L-n+1)th node from start. So first count nodes, then walk again to the predecessor and bypass the target.
approaches.theory: First traversal computes L in O(L). Target index from start is L-n. Use a dummy node before head so predecessor always exists, even when deleting head. Second traversal moves L-n steps from dummy, then does prev.next = prev.next.next. Two sequential linear passes remain O(L).

timeComplexity.explanation: Two linear traversals over L nodes: O(L) to count + O(L-n) to reach predecessor. Total O(L) time.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only a few pointers and dummy node, no extra allocation proportional to input.

steps: Target predecessor steps from dummy = L-n = 3, so dummy->1->2->3 lands on node 3

edgeCases: Remove head: [1,2,3], n=3 -> [2,3], dummy avoids null predecessor
Single node: [1], n=1 -> [], dummy.next becomes null
n equals length vs n=1 covers both ends

approaches.name: Approach 2: One-Pass Two Pointers with Gap
approaches.intuition: Maintain a gap of n nodes between fast and slow pointers. When fast hits the end, slow is exactly at the predecessor of the node to delete. This finds the target in one pass without knowing length.
approaches.theory: Start both fast and slow at dummy. Advance fast n+1 steps so gap = n+1 (accounts for dummy offset). Then move both together until fast == null. Invariant: distance(fast,slow)=n+1, so slow lands on (L-n)th node from dummy, the predecessor. Delete via slow.next = slow.next.next. Correct by gap invariant and dummy sentinel handling head deletion.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single pass: fast moves L+1 steps total, slow moves L-n steps. O(L) time with one traversal.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two pointers plus dummy node, constant extra space.

steps: Advance fast n+1=3 steps: fast at node 2

edgeCases: Remove head: [1,2,3], n=3 -> fast moves 4 steps to node 2, then both shift to fast=null, slow=dummy, delete head correctly
Single node: [1], n=1 -> fast moves 2 steps to null, loop skipped, dummy.next deleted -> []
Two nodes remove last: [1,2], n=1 -> slow ends at 1, bypass 2
Guaranteed valid n avoids null dereference when advancing fast n+1 steps
